question.worked_solution:
For this integral, we choose $u=4{x}^{4}+2$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}.$ Filling in our table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4{x}^{4}+2$ | ${e}^{x}$ |  |  |
| $16{x}^{3}$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $+$ | $(4{x}^{4}+2){e}^{x}$ |
| $48{x}^{2}$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $-$ | $-16{x}^{3}{e}^{x}$ |
| $96x$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $+$ | $48{x}^{2}{e}^{x}$ |
| $96$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $-$ | $-96x{e}^{x}$ |
| $0$ | ${e}^{x}$ | $+$ | $96{e}^{x}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{x}^{4}+2){e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{x}(4{x}^{4}-16{x}^{3}+48{x}^{2}-96x+98)+C\end{aligned}
$$
